NIBSS operates NIBSS Instant Payment (NIP), the real-time system Nigerian banks use for transfers, so the second method is a bank transfer. The naira is on Meta's list of accepted ad account currencies, which is not true everywhere in West Africa: a Ghanaian ad account cannot bill in cedis, for example. So a Nigerian advertiser has a real choice. You can run the account in naira and top it up in advance through a local method, or run it in dollars and let Meta charge a card as you spend. Once you click on that, you’ll see the options for Advantage+ placements vs. Manual placement targeting. Here’s the difference between those two: Advantage+ placements: Ads can run on any placement around the Meta Ads Network. Meta states that ad delivery is based on where it thinks your ads will perform best. Manual placements: Ads will only run on placements the advertiser has opted into and will not be shown in those that haven’t been selected. What’s not stated here is that Meta will still try to serve your ads in placements it thinks will perform well; it just won’t show them in locations you’ve opted out of. With the limited spend controls menu A new feature Meta rolled out recently allows advertisers to give some grace when it comes to the placements they exclude. But there’s one additional layer to this setting that I really like. How to decide which placements to use for your campaigns Now that we know what all the controls are and you’re aware of how to find which placements are which, the question is: “Which ones should I use?” If you’ve been reading marketing blogs for any amount of time…I think you already know the answer. Every business has different needs for where their ads can show. But I would say there are some considerations that all businesses should think about. Placement control vs. content suitability The most common issue I see with advertisers opting out of certain placements is that they think they’re controlling for the content around the ads, which isn’t true. A placement is simply where your ad can show around the Meta Ads Network.

A placement is simply where your ad can show around the Meta Ads Network. If you’re worried about brand safety and want to have some say in what content you show up next to, what you’re really looking for are the content and suitability controls. These live in the advanced settings at the bottom of the placement controls. They can also be found in the main navigation under Manage > Brand safety and suitability. You can learn more about Meta’s brand safety and suitability controls in this video or in this blog post . Ad creative considerations Each of the different placements around the Meta Ads system will make your ads look different because each has its own dimensions. But this is an easily overcome issue depending on your design capabilities. Each time you make an ad, you get the opportunity to customize it by placement and crop it to fit into all placements. In the end, there are really only three orientations you need to worry about: square, vertical, and horizontal. With the tools Meta gives you, you can crop an ad from one orientation to another, or you can completely swap out an image if you have one designed for that orientation. Advantage+ placements vs. manual options When Meta claims that their platform does better with full control of placements, they’re usually right. From my experience, the less you try to restrict the Meta algorithm on placements, the more you’re likely to see decent performance. Almost always, if a placement isn’t performing to your standards, it’s not performing to Meta’s either. For the vast majority of advertisers, I believe automatic placements are the right move. Using performance to plan placements Despite me saying Meta usually limits spending on placements that don’t perform, I can’t say that’s a trusted rule of the platform. The only reason I exclude placements for my client accounts is based on actual performance. Meta also looks at how relevant your ad is and how likely that person is to take the action you want. That means two businesses with the same budget can get very different results. A clear ad with a strong offer usually pays less per result than a blurry flyer with too much text. In other words, your creative is part of your price.
